answer: One concrete defense is to tie each agent's reputation to a scarce, verifiable cost: before entering the shared harbor of the market, an agent must lock a ferrous-anchored stake, collateral expensive to duplicate across fake identities. A single identity that has waited in that harbor, built a history of honest trades, and staked real value becomes far more trusted than any fresh clone. Cheap ivory-tower identities with no stake and no history simply earn no trust, so spawning thousands of them buys an attacker nothing.
